elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause (a): "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Same clause (a) expressly states "USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (b): "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (c) triggers on HDI processing "any data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company" — all categories, not selected data types — with "cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000".

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Clause (d): "workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Final sentence: "HDI shall provide certificates of insurance to the Company on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (b) requires E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000, which exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Clause (c) requires cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000, exceeding the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: Finding status "missing" is supported: the cited General Provisions run ends at 10.8 Headings; Counterparts with no insurance, coverage, or certificate obligation anywhere, and the vendor hosts the Site and handles Company data, so the rule applies.
All six preferred elements are met in operative language at the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence vs. aggregate) and party direction (HDI as insured obligor, Company as certificate recipient).

The cyber trigger is drafted to reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company rather than selected named data types, satisfying the Customer Data trigger requirement.

Minimality holds: the insertion is a concise new paragraph for a missing clause, drops the model language's "at its own expense" and one-year survival tail, adds no procedures, notice mechanics, additional-insured or waiver-of-subrogation extras, and deletes or paraphrases nothing outside the target elements (10.8 is retained verbatim).

Intent preserved: nothing in the existing Agreement is contradicted, no defined term is left undefined and no cross-reference dangles; the new paragraph is free-standing at the end of General Provisions. Minor housekeeping only — the rendered heading reads "Insurance." without the numbering (10.9) referenced in the rationale; confirm the section number is applied on execution.
Severity remains low per the rule, notwithstanding the walk-away framing in the rationale, because the redline fully cures the gap at the preferred level.
